posts.text:
A girl named Sarah went on a blind date and was really nervous. She worried he wouldn’t look anything like his photos.

Earlier that day, her neighbor Janet had given her some advice. “Relax,” she said. “There’s an app for that. It’s called ‘Mom, Are You OK?’ If the date’s bad, you pretend it’s an emergency call and make a quick exit.”

That evening, the doorbell rang.

Sarah took a deep breath and opened the door… and there he was — tall, handsome, and even better looking than his photos.

She smiled to herself. No need for the app.

Just as she was about to invite him in, his phone rang.

He looked at the screen, answered, and after a pause said, Mom? What’s wrong… are you okay?”

posts.author: The Drunk Republican
posts.text:
Political satire is fast approaching a dead end.

It is becoming increasingly difficult to lampoon the left, as they have become masters of lampooning themselves.

For someone who makes their hay on this app by mocking my political opponents, their decline into madness has become worrisome, albeit for very selfish reasons.

Shitposters such as myself operate in the gray area between reality and the outright absurd. It is here that we plant and harvest our little memes and clapbacks that have come to define online discourse.

But these days that fertile acreage has been decimated by the libs’ increasingly cartoonish behavior; the line between comedy and reality has beside blurred beyond distinction.

Consider that we are only a few years beyond the Me Too movement and woman-groping weirdo Pedro Pascal is now considered a leftist hero while successful model and actress Sydney Sweeney is dubbed a Nazi for wearing denim.

Or that a segment of the gay community believes they would be welcomed with open arms by Gazans.

Or that Jasmine Crockett exists.

I mean, what witty one-liners can possibly top these actual events?

There are none, just as no one or no thing  can outrun the speed of light. It’s physically fucking impossible.  

And I am but one man!

Should their Ls continue to pile up, as I predict they will, it’s difficult for me to find a path forward here. I could do food jokes I suppose (I’ve done one or two of those in the past to some acclaim). Or wade into philosophy and science, like a true intellectual.

But none of those are as fulfilling as dragging Commies through the proverbial mud.

So I say to them, “Return to me my fields, ye feckin’ weirdos!”

Don’t deny me my one true joy in life, I beg of you. Where is the humanity and compassion so beautifully expressed on your “Coexist” bumper stickers?

It’s not enough we must compete with AI, but now your cosmic neuroses, too?

Please, be slightly more normal. After all, are we not countrymen?

Do I not also bleed?

posts.author: 🇺🇸 Ronald Carter
posts.text:
I just got off the phone with someone who has tracked presidential communication patterns in Washington for over a decade. What they told me should end every "Trump is just posting memes" argument permanently.

"Every single president since Clinton had access to the same tools Trump is using right now. Every single one was briefed on the power of direct-to-public messaging. Every single one chose to route everything through press secretaries and managed press conferences because the political cost of being unfiltered was higher than the cost of being slow."

Trump posted 25 times on Truth Social in a single day. AI-generated imagery. Iran strike maps. Alien visuals. "I WANT YOU!" recruitment poster framing. "The clock is ticking, and they better get moving, FAST."

He chose to post that knowing the press would call it unhinged.

He chose to post that knowing late-night hosts would make it a punchline.

He chose to post that knowing foreign governments would screenshot every frame.

He chose to post that knowing his own allies would quietly ask him to stop.

A senior analyst I know who studies presidential signaling put it this way: "The difference between Trump and every president before him isn't access. They all had the same platforms. The difference is willingness."

Read that again.

Every president had the same ability to speak directly, visually, and without a filter to 100 million people. Only one actually does it — during a nuclear standoff, at 9 PM, with an AI-generated recruitment poster.

The meme is the message. The post is the policy signal. And most people are still treating it like a joke.

I'll keep you updated. Turn on notifications. 🚨
